title: http: optional check for ASCII headers
description:
Add a preference to check HTTP headers for non-ASCII, disabled by
default. When enabled, if non-ASCII is found when expecting a HTTP
header, then do not claim the packet as HTTP, thus allowing other
dissectors (including heuristics) a chance to parse the packet data.

notes.body:
So, I can see a case for this - say a capture with a number of different connections upgraded to Websocket on the default port, only some are captured in the middle of the connection (and you don't want to remove the default HTTP port from prefs).

But -1 is already used as a return value for "we need desegmentation but this looks like HTTP" and this will break desegmentation there and cause TCP to report dissector bugs. Similarly, this will cause some strange dissection of traffic that has been upgraded (because the offset isn't updated from the `call_dissector()` calls to the upgrade dissector.)

The SIP dissector has something similar, and there it uses a return value of -2 for "this is definitely not SIP"  distinguished from -1 for "this needs desegmentation."

If you're referring to the changes to `dissect_http_message()`, it already returned -1 for invalid HTTP messages, such as for too-short tvbuff or failure to reassemble headers. I just followed that convention with my additions. The return value of `dissect_http_message()` is never used as the return value from the dissector; it's only even checked in `dissect_http_on_stream()` and only added to the return value if it's not negative.

The difference is here:

```c
	return http_check_ascii_headers
		? offset
		: (int)tvb_captured_length(tvb);
```

which now means that if `dissect_http_message()` returns -1, now `dissect_http_on_stream()` returns the offset passed into `dissect_http_message()` instead of the entire tvb, causing it to report to TCP that the packet was rejected.

But `dissect_http_message()` returns -1 for packets that *are* HTTP but need defragmentation. What happens currently is that those packets still return `tvb_captured_length(tvb)` to TCP, accepting the packet, and set `pinfo->desegment_offset` and `pinfo->desegment_len`.

It's all part of how the HTTP dissector currently accepts anything that is on its configured ports, even if it doesn't look like HTTP. It only rejects frames when it's operating as a heuristic dissector.

In ef103b3986 `dissect_http_message()` returns -2 instead of -1 if the optional extra checks fail, and `dissect_http_on_stream()` checks for the -2 result and returns 0. I think this addresses the issue you mentioned with my original patch.
